sentences.text: Osmakasaurus is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur whose name means "canyon lizard" in the Lakota language.
The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered by Nelson Horatio Darton in 1896 in the Lakota Formation.
The type species O. depressus was originally described in 1909 by Charles W. Gilmore under the name Camptosaurus depressus.
In 2008, the species was reclassified into the genus Planicoxa as Planicoxa depressa before being assigned to the new genus Osmakasaurus in 2011.
Osmakasaurus belongs to the family Camptosauridae within the unranked group Iguanodontia.
This animal lived during the Early Cretaceous Valanginian age in what is now Buffalo Gap, South Dakota, USA, approximately 137 million years ago.

The Paleobiology Database records the time range for Osmakasaurus as extending from the Kimmeridgian to the Barremian (154.8 to 121.4 million years ago), which contradicts the specific Valanginian age mentioned elsewhere.
